subject: Pathology
title: Glomerular Diseases: Nephritic vs Nephrotic Syndromes
preview: Nephritic and nephrotic patterns overlap but emphasize different types of glomerular injury.

sections.title: Recognize the syndrome
points: Nephritic: dysmorphic erythrocytes or red-cell casts suggest glomerular inflammation.
Nephrotic: prominent proteinuria with hypoalbuminemia can cause generalized edema.

sections.title: Clinical correlations
points: Complement, infection history, autoimmune findings and renal function guide the differential.
Some glomerular disorders show mixed nephritic and nephrotic findings rather than clean textbook separation.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Do not diagnose a single glomerular disease solely from the syndrome label.
Edema by itself does not establish nephrotic syndrome.

quickRevision: Nephritic disease features inflammation with hematuria and often reduced filtration or raised blood pressure.
Nephrotic disease features heavy protein loss, edema and hypoalbuminemia, with variable lipid changes.
Kidney biopsy and additional tests are selected according to age, presentation and suspected cause.

quiz.question: What is a characteristic feature of nephrotic syndrome?
options: Absence of hypoalbuminemia in all cases
Predominant red-cell casts in every case
